blocks.text: I can read ‘The Journey’ and summarise the key events.
‘The Journey’ is a picture book by Francesca Sanna. Today you will explore the story and then tell it again in a short summary.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A person who has been forced to leave their country in order to escape war, violence or natural disaster.
To run away from a place or situation of danger.
A geographical line separating two countries.
To pull out the key events and ideas from a text.

blocks.text: ‘The Journey’ is a children’s **picture book**. It tells the story of two young girls who are fleeing their war-torn country to find a safe place to live.

items.title: Illustrator
items.sub: Francesca Sanna drew the pictures too

blocks.text: The book is inspired by true stories of {refugees} that the author met. She wanted to share the personal stories of the refugees we hear about on the news.
The story is told by a young girl. We never find out her name, so she is **unnamed**. She tells us about her family’s escape from their country.

items.title: Their mother
items.sub: goes on the journey and keeps the girls safe

blocks.text: The two girls and their mother are all {refugees}.
A refugee and a migrant are not the same thing.

items.title: Refugee
items.sub: has to leave because it is no longer safe to stay

items.title: Migrant
items.sub: moves to another place, usually to find work or better living conditions

blocks.q: Why did the girls and their mother leave their country?
options: They chose to go for a new job
They had to leave to escape war and find a safe place
They wanted a holiday by the sea
blocks.why: They are refugees: they were forced to leave to escape war and find somewhere safe to live.

blocks.text: Francesca Sanna does not say which countries the family are fleeing from or going to. We only know they are refugees looking for safety.

blocks.q: Does ‘The Journey’ tell us which country the family are going to?
options: Yes, it says they are going to England
No, the author does not say which country
Yes, it names the country in the last page
blocks.why: The author does not say which countries the characters flee from or go to. We only know they are looking for a safe place to live.

blocks.text: At the start, the girl lives happily with her family in a city close to the sea.

items: Then a war begins in her country.
The war changes the family’s lives forever.
Their mother decides to flee to take the girls to a safer place.

blocks.label: Why does the mother want to leave?
blocks.text: She wants to take her daughters to a **safer** place, away from the war.
The family travel for a long time. When they arrive at the {border}, they are banned from crossing.

items: They have to hide in the forest overnight.
They stay hidden until they pay someone to help them.

blocks.q: What happens when the family reach the border?
options: The border police let them cross straight away
They are banned from crossing and hide in the forest overnight
They turn around and go back home
blocks.why: They are banned from crossing the border, so they hide in the forest overnight until they pay someone to help them.

blocks.text: The last part of the journey is not easy either.

items: They have a challenging ferry crossing over rough seas with fellow refugees.
Then they take a train through many countries.
They travel closer and closer to a new, safe home. Birds follow the train, and they are moving to a new place too.

blocks.label: Do they arrive?
blocks.text: Not yet! The story ends with the family getting closer to a safe home where they hope to arrive soon.

blocks.q: Put each key event in the right part of the story.

items.text: A war begins and lives change forever
Mother decides to flee to a safer place

blocks.text: To {summarise} means to pull out the **key events and ideas** from a text. Summarising helps us build our understanding of the story and the meaning behind it.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Summarising does **not** mean describing every event in detail. Pick the important parts and keep it short.

options: It tells the story of a family’s holiday by the sea.
It tells the story of two young girls who are fleeing their war-torn country to find a safe place to live.
It lists everything that happens on every single page.

items.q: Which of these is a key event in the story?
options: The family are banned from crossing the border and hide in the forest.
The family visit a theme park.

blocks.q: Match each key word to its meaning.

pairs.b: a person forced to leave their country to escape war, violence or natural disaster
to run away from a place or situation of danger
a geographical line separating two countries
to pull out the key events and ideas from a text

slides.title: Engaging with the plot of ‘The Journey’

items: ‘The Journey’ is a children’s picture book by Francesca Sanna, who is both the author and the illustrator.
It is about two girls and their mother, who are {refugees} fleeing their war-torn country to find a safe place to live.
The family face many obstacles and challenges, including a border they are banned from crossing.
The story ends with them getting closer to a safe home where they hope to arrive soon.
Summarising the key events helps us build our understanding of the text and its meaning.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Engaging with the plot of ‘The Journey’
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word or a short phrase. Use what you learned about ‘The Journey’ by Francesca Sanna.

questions.prompt: Which word means to run away from a place or situation of danger?
questions.explanation: To flee means to run away from a place or situation of danger.

questions.prompt: What is the word for a geographical line separating two countries?
questions.explanation: A border is a geographical line separating two countries.

questions.prompt: Which word means to pull out the key events and ideas from a text?
questions.explanation: To summarise is to pull out the key events and ideas from a text.

questions.prompt: What do we call a person who has been forced to leave their country to escape war, violence or natural disaster?
questions.explanation: That is the meaning of a refugee.
Francesca Sanna is both the author and the illustrator.

questions.prompt: Who tells the story of ‘The Journey’: the girl, her sister or her mother?
questions.explanation: The story is told from the perspective of an unnamed young girl.

questions.prompt: Who goes on the journey with the two girls and keeps them safe?
questions.explanation: The mother goes on the journey with the girls and keeps them safe.

questions.prompt: Where do the family hide overnight after they are banned from crossing the border?
questions.explanation: They hide in the forest overnight until they pay someone to help them.

questions.prompt: Which vehicle do the family take through many countries at the end of the story?
questions.explanation: They take a train through many countries and travel closer to a safe home.

questions.prompt: True or false? The family tried to stay in their country and did not leave.
questions.explanation: Their mother decided to flee their country to take them to a safer place.
